# Additional public protocol facts

The development still-capture event ledger uses the numeric event meanings
DeviceInfoChanged (0x4008) and Nikon LiveViewStateChanged (0xC10C), cross-checked
against the upstream [libgphoto2 v2.5.31 protocol header](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/v2.5.31/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h).
No libgphoto2 implementation, header body or linked library is copied or used.
These entries are protocol identifiers, not a new transport dependency.

Before shutter dispatch these notifications require the read-only capture
profile to be checked again. They never attribute an image. After dispatch
they fail the transaction rather than silently accepting a changed state.
Unknown events, image/card object events and reset/removal notifications are
not treated as harmless property notifications.

The #343 follow-up also cross-checks StoreAdded (0x4004) against the same
header and the upstream [event handler](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/v2.5.31/camlibs/ptp2/library.c#L6923-L6928).
The identifier denotes storage addition, not image arrival. This application's
policy (not an upstream guarantee) is to invalidate the pre-shutter baseline,
re-read the existing Live-off/JPEG Fine/FX L profile once, then check two more
event batches. A further invalidation, any pending image/completion, removal,
reset or unknown event stops before shutter. StoreAdded after shutter is
terminal. No storage inventory/cache, filesystem reset implementation, setting
writer or image-attribution rule is copied from upstream.

The development preview lifecycle also references the numeric Nikon response
NotLiveView (0xA00B) in that public protocol header and prohibition bits 8
(battery exhausted) and 17 (temperature) in the same version's
[library.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/v2.5.31/camlibs/ptp2/library.c).
These are protocol facts only. No libgphoto2 implementation is copied or linked;
no setting writer, automatic retry or restart loop is adopted.

Capture diagnostics reference standard BatteryLevel (0x5001), FocusMode
(0x500A), ExposureTime (0x500D) and Nikon OutOfFocus (0xA002) identifiers
in that same public header. Read-only integer values are logged without
inferring optical focus, exposure completion or image ownership. No upstream
implementation or camera-setting writer is copied.

The explicit #337 state diagnostic adds read-only InfoDispErrStatus (0xD1B2),
ApplicationMode (0xD1F0), LiveViewSelector (0xD1A6), RecordingMedia (0xD10B)
and standard ExposureProgramMode (0x500E). Identifiers and scalar types are
cross-checked against the public libgphoto2
[protocol header](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h)
and [configuration definitions](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c).
The selector byte is also read by the fixed-commit digiCamControl NikonBase
referenced in NOTICE. These values do not identify every possible refusal;
zero error/prohibition must never authorize a refused Start. No upstream
implementation, settings writer, recovery loop or linked library is adopted.

The #416 stage A read-only settings display (`--settings-read-diagnostics` and the
"両台の設定を読む" button) reads these property descriptions with
GetDevicePropDesc (0x1014), plus the Live state with GetDevicePropValue (0x1015,
code 0xD1A2, already used above). All numbers below were checked on 2026-11-10
against the public libgphoto2 sources at the fixed commit
`92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab`: protocol header
[ptp.h](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h),
[config.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c)
and [ptp-pack.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp-pack.c).
No implementation, header body or linked library is copied or used; these are
protocol identifiers and value meanings only. This step writes nothing: 0x1016
(SetDevicePropValue, ptp.h#L245) stays refused by the read-only gate.

The DevicePropDesc layout parsed by `ParseD810PropDesc` (property code u16, data
type u16, get/set u8, default, current, form flag u8, then range min/max/step or an
enumeration count u16 and values, little endian; get/set 0 = Get, 1 = GetSet;
form flag 0 = none, 1 = range, 2 = enumeration) follows
[ptp-pack.c#L660-L734](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp-pack.c#L660-L734),
the data type numbers [ptp.h#L1911-L1935](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1911-L1935)
and the flags [ptp.h#L4123-L4139](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L4123-L4139).
Unlike the upstream unpacker, which tolerates short or surplus data, this
application requires the exact computed length and refuses strings, arrays and
other widths.

Not established by these sources: which of 0xD054 and 0xD16A a D810 answers to,
whether 0xD100 exists on it, and (with libgphoto2 alone) the real scalar type
of 0xD200: the #427 section below takes UINT16 from digiCamControl, which is
one source (未照合 on a body). Whether each source line really belongs to the D810 rather
than another Nikon body is likewise not established: the upstream tables are
per-vendor, not per-model. The diagnostic prints each code's answer for a person
to compare with the body.

## #416 white balance and metering in the settings copy (ADR-0038 revision)

The ADR-0038 revision, which the owner decided to adopt, adds white balance (0x5005) and the metering mode (0x500B) to the items the settings copy plan covers. The fixed product table enables CAM-B's rows for both (CAM-A's rows stay disabled). Neither has been written on a real body (未検証). The numbers below were read in the same public libgphoto2 sources at the fixed commit `92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab` as the table above: [ptp.h](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h), [config.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c) and [ptp.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.c). No implementation, header body or linked library is copied or used; these are protocol identifiers and value meanings only. No Nikon SDK material is used.

| Fact | Code / value | Source lines |
| --- | --- | --- |

| White balance kinds that lean on content held in the body, never copied | 0x0001 Manual, 0x0003 One-push Automatic; Nikon 0x8012 Color Temperature, 0x8013 Preset | [config.c#L1455](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L1455), [config.c#L1457](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L1457), [config.c#L1464-L1465](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L1464-L1465) |

| Nikon vendor operations that measure a white (not used) | 0x9402-0x9406 | [ptp.h#L623-L627](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L623-L627) |

What these sources do not establish:

- A way to copy the content of a registered white (Preset). The properties that hold it (0xD025-0xD029) have no put function upstream and no stated unit; 0xD01F is a slot number; the operations that measure a white are vendor operations, which the application does not send. So the content of a Preset cannot be copied on the strength of public sources (未成立).
- The scalar type and unit of colour temperature 0xD01E: it has a name in ptp.h and ptp.c but no entry in config.c (未照合). It is not written.
- Whether a D810 answers to these properties, and with which GetSet: not established by these sources (未検証 until a read on the real bodies; the stage A read already shows it per property).
- What the spot metering position follows: no property for it was found in these sources, so a metering mode copy does not carry a position.

## #416 further image-look properties (identifiers for a Proposed design, nothing is read or written for them)

The ADR-0038 revision draft that lists the settings of a Camera Control Pro 2 style screen names the properties below. They are cited from the same fixed commit as above ([ptp.h](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h), [config.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c)). The upstream tables are per vendor, and the value tables of Active D-Lighting and High ISO noise reduction are filled in with another body's values (config.c#L12560-L12565, the generic list), so none of these is established for a D810 (未照合). No implementation is copied or used.

The range of settings a PC control program offers was taken from the manufacturer's public Camera Control Pro 2 online help (English), pages 08_camera_controls_01 to 08_camera_controls_05 and 10_camera_menu_01 under https://nikonimglib.com/ccp2/onlinehelp/en/. Only setting names and the cameras a page names are used, to decide which settings are ordinary shooting settings. The help does not name protocol operations, so it says nothing about how the program talks to the camera (未確認).



## #416 sources for the settings write (ADR-0038 stage B prerequisite 8)

This section records where the numbers, the response meaning and the procedures behind the settings write come from. The public sources are the libgphoto2 files at the fixed commit `92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab` ([ptp.h](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h), [config.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c), [ptp.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.c), [ptp-pack.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp-pack.c)) and the digiCamControl [NikonBase.cs](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs) at the fixed commit `a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312` (file SHA-256 in [digicamcontrol-NOTICE.txt](digicamcontrol-NOTICE.txt)). No implementation, header body or linked library is copied or used. Nothing here is taken from Nikon SDK material. Where a line says 未確認 (not checked), no public source recorded here establishes it.

### Rule for a body's answer

A read on the real body may only choose one code from the candidates that a public source above names, and confirm that its type, GetSet and form fit. It never adds a code, a type or a meaning that no public source names, and the application never switches to the other candidate at run time (ADR-0038 decision 13).

### Response code 0x200A

| Fact | Source lines |
| --- | --- |
| 0x200A is `PTP_RC_DevicePropNotSupported`, in the run of standard PTP response codes (0x2002 GeneralError to 0x200B InvalidObjectFormatCode). 0x2019 is `PTP_RC_DeviceBusy` | [ptp.h#L1119-L1129](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1119-L1129) (0x200A at [ptp.h#L1128](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1128)), [ptp.h#L1143](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1143) |

- The name and the number come from the upstream header. The clause of the PTP standard (ISO 15740) that defines the code was not checked: 未確認.
- The application's own policy, not an upstream statement: a code in 0x2002-0x2FFF or 0xA000-0xAFFF (0x2019 excluded) is an explicit refusal. That a body means "this property is not offered" when it refuses the END of a transfer whose begin was accepted with a size of 0 is an inference from the name and the shape. No public source recorded here describes that shape: 未確認.

### ISO auto control: two candidates, and how one is chosen

| Fact | Source lines |
| --- | --- |
| Two property codes are named for Nikon ISO auto control: 0xD054 (`PTP_DPC_NIKON_ISOAuto`) and 0xD16A (`PTP_DPC_NIKON_ISO_Auto`) | [ptp.h#L2397](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L2397), [ptp.h#L2596](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L2596) |
| Both have their own entry in the upstream configuration table, with the same UINT8 type and the same on/off get and put functions (a nonzero value shows as On; the get function requires a range form) | [config.c#L12088-L12089](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12088-L12089), [config.c#L1228-L1256](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L1228-L1256) |
| Upstream offers an entry only when the body's DeviceInfo lists the property code, so a body can offer one of the two | [config.c#L57-L92](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L57-L92), [config.c#L12717-L12718](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12717-L12718) |

- Selection on this model: the stage A read (read only) got a response to 0xD054, and 0xD16A was answered with a failed begin and an END refused with 0x200A (the size of 0 is an inference). 0xD100 has not been read on a body: 未確認. The write path reads neither of the two. The fixed product table confirms 0xD054 (never 0xD16A) for ISO auto control, with its rows disabled. The choice follows the rule above: the code has a name in a public source and the body answered it.
- Not established by public sources: that 0xD054 is the body's ISO auto setting (the name `ISOAuto` and the on/off mapping are upstream's), and which Nikon bodies use 0xD054 or 0xD16A. Comparing the body's own menu with the reading is the only check, and no result of it is recorded here: 未確認.
- 0xD100 (shutter speed, Nikon): the code is named at [ptp.h#L2522](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L2522), but the encoding of its value (Bulb and Time marks, unit) is not recorded in any source here. Only 0x500D, whose encoding is in the stage A table above, may be confirmed for writing; the fixed product table confirms it. CAM-B's row is enabled in stage 3 (CAM-A's row stays disabled), and 0xD100 is never in the table.

### ChangeCameraMode (0x90C2) is not sent

| Fact | Source lines |
| --- | --- |
| Name and number: `PTP_OC_NIKON_ChangeCameraMode` 0x90C2, one parameter, no data | [ptp.h#L583](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L583), [ptp.h#L4975](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L4975) |
| Upstream sends it with the given mode in a "Nikon control mode" setting, and with mode 1 before it sets the exposure program to M and the exposure time to Bulb | [config.c#L8512-L8527](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L8512-L8527), [config.c#L9735-L9745](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L9735-L9745) |
| digiCamControl names it the same way and sends 1 (lock) and 0 (unlock) | [NikonBase.cs#L66](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L66), [NikonBase.cs#L2321-L2331](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L2321-L2331) |

- These sources show that other programs send 0x90C2 before some writes. They do not say what the parameter does on a D810, or whether a D810 needs it before the exposure mode is written: 未確認.
- ADR-0038 does not permit it: [DECISIONS.md](../docs/DECISIONS.md), the scope principle ("command" item), decision 2 and decision 14. The write gate admits 0x90C8, 0x1014, 0x1015 and 0x1016 only, and the contract tests send 0x90C2 to both gates and expect a refusal. If a write turns out to need 0x90C2 or another vendor operation, the copy stops and the owner decides.

### Write order is a design decision

- No public source recorded here defines an order across properties. The order is a decision of ADR-0038 (decisions 4, 5 and 14). The table order of `kD810WriteItems` in the code is the write order: exposure mode, ISO auto control (Off), ISO, shutter speed, aperture, and then, under the ADR-0038 revision, white balance and metering.
- Reason given in the ADR: the exposure mode and the ISO auto control come first because ISO, shutter speed and aperture are written only after the body is read as M with ISO auto Off (decision 4). No dependency is recorded between ISO, shutter speed and aperture, so their relative order is a convenience, not a requirement.
- The one upstream sequence seen writes the exposure mode before the exposure time ([config.c#L9735-L9745](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L9735-L9745)). It is a single Bulb routine and is not the source of the order.
- The per-camera order of the Proposed settings screen (CAM-B first, CAM-A last) is a design proposal with no upstream source. It is not implemented: the copy writes CAM-B only.

## #427 more rows for the read-only comparison

The comparison of the two bodies reads six more properties, reads the Picture Control item with another scalar type, and names the values of four rows. It stays read-only: GetDevicePropDesc (0x1014) exactly as in stage A, no 0x1016, no vendor operation. The six new rows are the `extended` rows of `kD810SettingSpecs`. The write path still reads only the ten fixed rows (`kD810WriteReadSpecs`, ten entries by `static_assert`) and writes none of the new ones. Sources are the same fixed commits as above: libgphoto2 `92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab` and digiCamControl `a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312` (`NikonBase.cs`, SHA-256 `4328ec2fb6f31fc4b1cd04d643d2dd8aa2e7ade72c9bd4f37a083e9b0975abbc`, listed in digicamcontrol-NOTICE.txt).

### Rule for a row

A property code gets a row only when the property list that a D810 reported contains it: [cameras/nikon-d810.txt#L85-L297](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/cameras/nikon-d810.txt#L85-L297) at the fixed commit (SHA-256 `ad89322d582a9568571032acfd1107e66071839ea6903c487e56c758c8aefef6`; the "Device Properties Supported" block, 212 codes). The list is one dump of one body. It records a device version of V0.23, so which firmware produced it is not known (※未確認), and its serial field is not repeated here. 0xD16A is not in the list; 0xD054 and 0xD100 are. That matches the stage A notes above (0xD16A refused, 0xD054 answered).

Why the rule: a body that does not know a property may answer the begin with a transfer context of size 0 and then refuse the END, which stops the read session (the tests keep this shape: `UnsupportedIsoAutoCandidateIsLast`, `ExtendedRowFailures`). 0xD16A stays the last row for that reason, and the extended rows come after the ten fixed rows, so a stop in an extended row leaves the ten read as before.

The list says that a D810 reported the code. It gives no type and no value table. The types and names below come from the generic upstream tables, which are per vendor and not per model: libgphoto2 has no D810 table (the D810 USB id 0x0436 is at [library.c#L1775](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/library.c#L1775); the capture settings fall to the generic menus, [config.c#L12627](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12627)). A body that answers with another scalar type shows as `type_mismatch` for that row, with the type it returned in the log line; the application never coerces.

| HDR mode | 0xD130 | [nikon-d810.txt#L243](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/cameras/nikon-d810.txt#L243) | UINT8: [config.c#L12234](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12234). `NikonBase.cs` declares `sbyte` ([NikonBase.cs#L662-L678](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L662-L678)), so the sources disagree on signedness; the table follows libgphoto2. The same disagreement exists for 0xD14E (UINT8 in the generic menu, [config.c#L12564](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12564), `sbyte` in [NikonBase.cs#L681-L700](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L681-L700)), where the table already uses UINT8. A body that answers INT8 shows as `type_mismatch`. | 0 OFF, 1 ON: both sources ([NikonBase.cs#L662-L678](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L662-L678) also has 2 "ON (sequence)", which stays raw). |
| Active D-Lighting (unchanged type, still raw) | 0xD14E | [nikon-d810.txt#L249](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/cameras/nikon-d810.txt#L249) | UINT8 (see above) | Raw. The two upstream tables run in opposite order for two body families ([config.c#L7589-L7607](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L7589-L7607): 0 Extra high to 5 Auto, and 0 Auto to 5 Extra high), no source ties either to the D810, and `NikonBase.cs` gives the first order only by inheritance ([NikonBase.cs#L681-L700](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L681-L700)). |

Value 0 of the on/off rows is named only because both sources agree. A name is shown only when two sources agree, or, for Picture Control, when it is the one public table of the Nikon driver the D810 class inherits (a deliberate exception for the one row whose names the comparison needs; the raw value is always in the log line). Anything else is shown as `raw 0x…`; equality is always decided on the raw value, never on a name.

### In the D810 list, not added

| Code | Property | Why not |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 0xD201, 0xD141, 0xD150, 0xD20D | Picture Control change, type of automatic WB, colour temperature tune, electronic front curtain | Only a name in ptp.h: no type and no values, so a row would be a guess. |
| 0xD017 to 0xD01D | Fine adjustment per WB kind | The scalar type differs by body ([config.c#L2241-L2320](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L2241-L2320): INT8, UINT8 or UINT16), and one value covers one axis only, so a match would not show that the other axis matches. |
| 0xD01E, 0xD01F | Colour temperature, preset number | The sources disagree on the type and unit of 0xD01E. A matching preset number (0xD01F, UINT8 in [config.c#L12348](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12348)) says nothing about the content of the preset, which a PC cannot read here; the row would look like a match that is not one. |
| 0xD131, 0xD132 | HDR exposure deviation, intensity | Matter only while HDR is on, which the HDR row shows. The only value tables are in `NikonBase.cs` ([NikonBase.cs#L618-L660](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L618-L660), `sbyte`). |
| 0xD031 | JPEG compression policy | Only in the table of another body ([config.c#L12545](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12545), the D3s table). |
| 0xD030, 0xD056, 0xD06A, 0x5013 | Image area, EV step, exposure delay, release mode | Not image processing; the image area is already checked by the capture precheck; the exposure delay tables contradict each other between two driver classes. |
| 0xD010, 0xD040 | Shooting menu bank, custom setting bank | No type and no values. |

### What stays unread

The Picture Control adjustments (sharpening, contrast, saturation and so on), the content of the WB presets and the green-magenta WB fine adjustment are not properties a read of these codes shows (digiCamControl reads the Picture Control adjustments with the vendor operation 0x90CC, [NikonBase.cs#L369-L407](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L369-L407), which the application does not send). The colour temperature value in kelvin (0xD01E, listed above as not read) is not compared either: when both bodies' white balance is the colour temperature kind, the WB row reads the same whatever the kelvin values are. The screen therefore says that "everything matches" covers the table's rows only, and names the colour temperature value among what was not compared.

## #426 AF frame move (ChangeAfArea 0x9205) and the AF frame words of the Live View frame header

This section records where the AF frame operation and the frame header words of the development preview come from. The public sources are the libgphoto2 files at the fixed commit `92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab` ([ptp.h](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h), [config.c](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c)) and the digiCamControl files at the fixed commit `a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312` ([NikonBase.cs](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs), file SHA-256 in [digicamcontrol-NOTICE.txt](digicamcontrol-NOTICE.txt); [NikonD600Base.cs](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonD600Base.cs); [LiveViewViewModel.cs](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl/ViewModel/LiveViewViewModel.cs)). No implementation, header body or linked library is copied or used. Nothing here is taken from Nikon SDK material. Where a line says 未確認 (not checked), no public source recorded here establishes it.

| Fact | Source lines |
| --- | --- |
| `PTP_OC_NIKON_ChangeAfArea` is 0x9205 with 2 parameters; it is sent as a command without a data phase | [ptp.h#L604](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L604), [ptp.h#L5024](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L5024) |
| The comment above that macro says "starts movie capture"; it is a copy of the neighbouring macro's text and contradicts the macro under it. The macro (operation, 2 parameters x and y) is what is used | [ptp.h#L5013-L5024](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L5013-L5024) |
| Upstream takes the position as the text `XxY`, parses two integers and sends them unchanged. No range, origin or unit is written down | [config.c#L8383-L8385](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L8383-L8385) |
| Upstream names the response NotLiveView (0xA00B) as "works only in LiveView mode" | [config.c#L8386-L8388](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L8386-L8388), [ptp.h#L1172](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1172) |
| Upstream does not wait after the move; its waiting code is disabled | [config.c#L8392-L8404](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L8392-L8404) (`#if 0`) |
| Upstream offers the setting only when the body's DeviceInfo lists the operation | [config.c#L11894](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L11894), [config.c#L12797-L12800](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/config.c#L12797-L12800) |
| Response names: OutOfFocus 0xA002, InvalidStatus 0xA004, NotLiveView 0xA00B (names only; the sources do not say when this operation answers with which) | [ptp.h#L1163](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1163), [ptp.h#L1165](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1165), [ptp.h#L1172](https://github.com/gphoto/libgphoto2/blob/92171a382f185f617e95cb9acecf2d43688b19ab/camlibs/ptp2/ptp.h#L1172) |
| digiCamControl sends the same operation with the two values as UINT32, without a DeviceReady before it (the call is commented out) | [NikonBase.cs#L59](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L59), [NikonBase.cs#L2104-L2110](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonBase.cs#L2104-L2110) |
| Header words (D810 inherits from the D600 base): live image size at offsets 8 and 10, `ImageWidth` and `ImageHeight` at 12 and 14, AF frame size at 24 and 26, AF frame centre `FocusX` and `FocusY` at 28 and 30, `Focused = result[48] != 1`, orientation byte 37. The words are read with `ToInt16` (signed, big endian, the same reading as the level words at 52 and 56) | [NikonD600Base.cs#L154-L175](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl.Devices/Nikon/NikonD600Base.cs#L154-L175) |
| A click is converted to the operation's values by the ratio of `ImageWidth` and `ImageHeight` to the displayed size; the frame is drawn around `FocusX` and `FocusY` with `FocusFrameXSize` and `FocusFrameYSize`, in the same space | [LiveViewViewModel.cs#L2966-L2981](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl/ViewModel/LiveViewViewModel.cs#L2966-L2981), [LiveViewViewModel.cs#L2369-L2396](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl/ViewModel/LiveViewViewModel.cs#L2369-L2396) |

How the application uses them (its own decisions, not upstream statements):

- The position is taken as the centre of the frame, because the public driver draws the frame around `FocusX` and `FocusY`. The click is converted into the space of the header's `ImageWidth` and `ImageHeight` and moved inside by half the frame size, so that the frame lies in the image. The body's answer is shown back as the green frame; that comparison is the only check of the position.
- Header words that do not fit (an image size of zero or above a signed 16 bit word, an aspect ratio more than 2 percent away from the JPEG's, a frame larger than the image, a centre outside it) are treated as unknown and nothing is drawn or sent.
- The dedicated gate admits 0x9205 with exactly two UINT32 values below the image size of a header read less than two seconds earlier, and nothing else. 0x9206 (AF cancel), 0x9207, 0x90C2 and every property write stay refused there and in the unchanged Live View gate.
- The focus mark (byte 48) is displayed as the body's report only. It is not an optical focus decision.

Not established by these sources (未確認): that a D810 lists or accepts 0x9205; the actual values of `ImageWidth`, `ImageHeight`, the frame size and `FocusX`/`FocusY` on a D810 and their ratio to the JPEG; the origin of the coordinates and whether the point is the centre or a corner; whether the body's AF area mode (property 0xD05D, which the upstream header itself marks with a FIXME) decides if the frame can be moved; when this operation answers 0xA004 or 0xA00B; what byte 48 means on a D810; whether the zoom state of the Live View changes the coordinate space (digiCamControl acts on a click only for the full-frame view, [LiveViewWnd.xaml.cs#L149-L158](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl/windows/LiveViewWnd.xaml.cs#L149-L158)). The upstream click conversion and the frame drawing treat a flipped image differently from each other ([LiveViewViewModel.cs#L2976-L2977](https://github.com/dukus/digiCamControl/blob/a95ee52bbc1e192a7d1da038f3af6561b185d312/CameraControl/ViewModel/LiveViewViewModel.cs#L2976-L2977)); the preview does not rotate or flip its pictures and does not copy that handling. The first use on a body reads the words only (see [WPD_PREVIEW_FOCUS.md](../docs/WPD_PREVIEW_FOCUS.md)).

| Camera Control Pro 2 help (English, topic `04_live_view_01`; the page has no fixed version): for the bodies it lists, the Live View window shoots with "Shoot" and "AF and Shoot"; "AF and Shoot" does not release when focus is not achieved. The page does not say whether Live View continues after the shot | online help, no line anchor |
| D810 reference manual, printed page 36 (read in a third party's reprint; whether it is the same text as the official PDF is not checked): in Live View shooting the shutter can be released without focus. This is about the body's own button, not about a PC command | printed page 36 |

How the application uses them (its own decisions, not upstream statements):

- The probe sends `0x90C0` with `0xFFFFFFFF` once, with Live View open, the way digiCamControl does in the same state. It sends no `0x9207` and no AF. Whether a D810 accepts this in Live View is what the probe observes.
- Before the shot Live View must read on (0xD1A2 = 1), the quality JPEG Fine and the size 7360x4912. After it the probe reads DeviceReady until it is no longer busy, then events up to 15 seconds for one 0xC101, imports that one object (0x1008, 0x1009), and then observes the completion event for a bounded time. The import is done even for a probe because an image left in SDRAM prohibits Live View start (bit 12 above); the application never sends a delete.
- The event meanings are the ones above. After the shot a 0xC101 together with 0x4004, 0x4005, 0x4008, 0xC10C or a code with no name is recorded, and its image is kept only as a private partial. Two 0xC101, 0x4002 or an invalid handle: nothing is imported.
- After the shot 0xD1A2 is read once. When it reads on, the Live path reads one frame; otherwise no frame read is sent. Both Live sessions are then stopped; no Live View start is sent.

Not established by these sources (未確認): that a D810 accepts `0x90C0` while Live View is on; whether it runs AF at the shot or answers OutOfFocus; whether Live View continues after the shot; which events arrive and in which order (0xC10C is not in the D810 list); whether 0x90C7 answers during Live View and how many events pile up over a long Live View; what the body does with an imported SDRAM image when no delete is sent; whether the AF frame or the Live View magnification changes at the shot; whether the 10-minute automatic end (custom setting c4) restarts its clock at a shot.
